# Dashboard by Glassmkr

> Bare metal monitoring dashboard, AGPL-3.0-only and self-hostable. Alert rules, per-core CPU, SMART, IPMI, network diagnostics.

## Quick Start

Install the Crucible agent on your server. The bootstrap script supports Ubuntu
and Debian only and needs root plus a key:
```
curl -sf https://glassmkr.com/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --api-key gmk_cru_live_xxx
```
On RHEL, Rocky, Alma or Arch use the single-file binary instead, which needs no
Node (the installer and the binary do not support Alpine):
https://glassmkr.com/docs/getting-started

Sign up at https://app.glassmkr.com/register, add your server, configure the API key in /etc/glassmkr/crucible.yaml (legacy installs: /etc/glassmkr/collector.yaml; the agent reads either). Crucible pushes health snapshots every 5 minutes by default (interval_seconds, minimum 60).

## API Reference

Base URL: https://app.glassmkr.com/api/v1
Authentication: Bearer token. Account API access: gmk_acct_live_xxx (or legacy forge_xxx). Crucible ingest: gmk_cru_live_xxx (or legacy col_xxx).

### Server Management
- GET /servers - list all servers for authenticated customer
- GET /servers/:id - server details
- DELETE /servers/:id - remove server
- GET /servers/:id/health - latest snapshot with active alerts
- GET /servers/:id/alerts?status=active|all - alerts (active only or full history)
- GET /servers/:id/metrics?hours=24 - time-series data for charts (CPU, RAM, load, swap, network, per-core CPU)
- GET /servers/:id/history?hours=24 - raw snapshot history
- GET /servers/:id/analyses - AI analysis history (free; needs an LLM endpoint configured on self-hosted)
- POST /servers/:id/analyze - trigger new AI analysis (free; needs an LLM endpoint configured on self-hosted)

### Alert Management
- POST /alerts/:id/acknowledge - acknowledge an active alert
- GET /servers/:id/mutes - list muted rules for a server
- POST /servers/:id/mutes - mute a rule: { "alert_type": "interface_errors" }
- DELETE /servers/:id/mutes - unmute a rule: { "alert_type": "interface_errors" }

### Notification Channels
- GET /channels - list channels
- POST /channels - create channel: { "name": "ops", "channel_type": "telegram|slack|email", "config": { "chat_id": "123" } }
- PUT /channels/:id - update channel
- DELETE /channels/:id - delete channel
- POST /channels/:id/test - send test notification

### Billing (dormant: hosted has no paid tier; endpoints remain for legacy subscription management only)
- GET /billing/status - subscription status
- POST /billing/checkout - retired; answers 410 (no new subscription can be created)
- POST /billing/portal - Stripe customer portal
- GET /billing/token - MCP API token
- POST /billing/token/rotate - rotate token

### Ingest (Crucible)
- POST /ingest - push snapshot (Bearer gmk_cru_live_xxx or legacy col_xxx, rate limited to 1/min)
- GET /version - latest Crucible version info

## Alert Rules

The full catalogue, with the firing condition and remediation workflow for
each rule, is at https://glassmkr.com/docs/rules and as a machine map at
https://glassmkr.com/docs/rules/llms.txt. Every rule is listed below under the
priority its definition declares.

Priority P0 Critical (data already at risk):
- boot_config_broken, gpu_uncorrected_ecc, gpu_xid_critical, mce_uncorrected

Priority P1 Urgent (act now):
- accept_backlog_or_syn_flood, bond_slave_down, conntrack_exhaustion, cpu_temperature_high, disk_fill_projection, disk_io_errors, ecc_errors, fd_exhaustion, filesystem_readonly, gpu_driver_unsafe_reboot, gpu_thermal_critical, ipmi_fan_failure, ipmi_sel_critical, lacp_partner_lost, lvm_thinpool_metadata_high, mem_pressure_high, no_firewall, nvlink_link_down, nvme_critical_warning, oom_kills, psu_redundancy_loss, raid_degraded, server_unreachable, service_flapping, smart_failing, softnet_drops, ssh_root_password, systemd_service_failed, systemd_service_oom_killed, unexpected_reboot, zfs_pool_unhealthy, zfs_scrub_errors, zfs_slog_faulted

Priority P2 High (fix within hours):
- clock_drift, cpu_high, cpu_iowait_high, cpu_pressure_high, disk_space_high, drive_smart_unreadable, gpu_pcie_link_degraded, gpu_power_cap_throttling, inode_high, interface_errors, io_pressure_high, kernel_needs_reboot, kernel_vulnerabilities, link_speed_mismatch, listen_overflow, ntp_not_synced, nvme_wear_high, os_end_of_life, pending_security_updates, ssh_config_unapplied, swap_high, tcp_retrans_high

Priority P3 Medium (fix within days):
- bios_firmware_age, boot_config_drift, cmos_battery_low, disk_latency_high, gpu_corrected_ecc_storm, gpu_driver_or_firmware_drift, interface_saturation, ipmi_monitoring_unavailable, ipmi_sel_full, load_high, memory_channels_underpopulated, ram_high, unattended_upgrades_disabled

P4 Low is not declared by any rule. It marks a proactive recommendation, or an
alert whose instance severity is informational, and shows on the dashboard
without paging: channels receive P0 through P3 unless configured otherwise.

## Snapshot Payload Structure

Crucible sends this JSON to POST /ingest every 5 minutes:
- system: { hostname, ip, os, kernel, uptime_seconds }
- cpu: { user_percent, system_percent, iowait_percent, idle_percent, load_1m, load_5m, load_15m, cores: [{ core, user_percent, system_percent, iowait_percent, idle_percent, irq_percent, softirq_percent }] }
- memory: { total_mb, used_mb, available_mb, swap_total_mb, swap_used_mb }
- disks: [{ device, mount, total_gb, used_gb, percent_used, fstype, options, inodes_total, inodes_used, inodes_free }]
- smart: [{ device, model, health, temperature_c, percentage_used, reallocated_sectors, pending_sectors, power_on_hours }]
- network: [{ interface, speed_mbps, rx_bytes_sec, tx_bytes_sec, rx_errors, tx_errors, rx_drops, tx_drops }]
- raid: [{ device, level, status, degraded, disks, failed_disks }]
- ipmi: { available, sensors: [{ name, value, unit, status }], ecc_errors: { correctable, uncorrectable }, fans: [{ name, rpm, status }] }
- os_alerts: { oom_kills_recent, zombie_processes, time_drift_ms }
- security: { ssh, firewall, pending_updates, kernel_vulns, kernel_reboot, auto_updates }

## For AI Agents

Dashboard is designed for programmatic access. An AI agent can:
1. Register a server via the dashboard (manual step, provides API key)
2. Install Crucible via SSH: curl -sf https://glassmkr.com/install.sh | bash
3. Query server health via GET /servers/:id/health
4. List and acknowledge alerts via GET /servers/:id/alerts and POST /alerts/:id/acknowledge
5. Mute noisy rules via POST /servers/:id/mutes
6. Trigger AI analysis via POST /servers/:id/analyze (free; needs an LLM endpoint configured on self-hosted)
7. Access metrics for charting via GET /servers/:id/metrics

MCP: this dashboard serves a first-party MCP endpoint at /mcp. Manage
connections and scopes at https://app.glassmkr.com/settings/mcp. Self-hosting it
needs TLS in front and a few environment variables; see
https://glassmkr.com/docs/mcp. The separate Bench project is archived and is no
longer the MCP path.
